questions.evidenceQuote: Hinds partnered with Mark Mortensen to survey forty-nine teams in the research and development division of a single multinational corporation. The results showed that geographically distributed teams had far less spontaneous communication, less shared identity, and far more task conflict than those in geographically concentrated teams. Hinds and Mortensen concluded that “spontaneous communication contributes to a shared identity, facilitates the creation of shared context, and aids distributed teams in identifying and resolving conflicts before they escalate.”

questions.evidenceQuote: Spontaneity poses another challenge when we try to make new friends in adulthood. What is the difference between college friends and post-college friends? Your post-college friends might be coworkers or the parents of your children’s friends.

specificFindings: Hinds and Mortensen are the quoted concluding researchers. Contributes,facilitates,aids retain supportive roles for identity,context and early conflict resolution, not a guarantee of identical decisions or no conflict.

Adult-friendship discussion contrasts proximity and repeated unplanned interaction with post-college settings. Spatial proximity differs from emotional closeness, and friend quantity differs from relationship depth.

Might be coworkers or childrens friends parents gives possible sources, not both required or the users actual family status. The closeness question is reflective rather than recorded personal history.

The essay title introduces reporter Alex Williams quotation. The question mark in the title does not end the full source attribution. His fatalism can creep in is a possible feeling, not a clinical finding or universal impossibility of adult friendship.
A shared project might create closeness; unless on a project again and hard to stay in touch describe difficulty without ruling out all other contact or declaring the earlier bond false.

If you have a partner introduces a conditional additional coordination factor in the authors discussion. It does not assert the reader has a partner or impose a general moral requirement on every relationship.

By ourselves adds independent spontaneous action rather than abandoning all friends. Jason DCruz is the philosopher using volatile reason; the excerpt does not provide the complete philosophical definition and none is invented.
Moritz is explicitly hypothetical, not a research participant. Original Berlin-to-Dresden tickets and friends expectations differ from the later option to remain aboard toward Zittau.
Dinner being prepared and shared concert tickets explain existing responsibilities. Could and if preserve the alternative as a possibility before the later spontaneous decision.
Right after leaving Dresden fixes the timing of euphoric freedom in the hypothetical story. It is not a measured clinical state of actual passengers or evidence every spontaneous act feels the same.

Spontaneity over responsibility summarises this particular trade-off. Once in a while limits the authors recommendation, without requiring cancellation of every commitment or guaranteeing no social cost.

Most of us and for a living introduce professional work. The authors literature,statistics and visualisation learning are a personal example, not a fixed method or current technology recommendation for all researchers.
Serious business is demanding work, not only commerce. Focus can reduce fun and laughter without proving focus worthless or every professional permanently unhappy.
The athlete examples retain recognised talent,determination and grit while describing loss of enjoyment. Might be one reason is not sole-cause proof or a fresh diagnosis of any named individual.

Other factors,such as and not just explicitly prevent reducing complex mental-health histories to seriousness alone. The examples are book-reported personal histories, not independently diagnosed causes or a universal account for every athlete.
The bottom line is the idiom for the main point that elite life is tough, not measured income or denial of achievement.
